objects.description: Memory-mapped register block for the ARM SysTick timer (CTRL, LOAD, VAL, CALIB). Intended to be accessed via the SYSTICK macro pointing to address 0xe000e010.
Memory-mapped register block for the Reset and Clock Control (RCC) peripheral of STM32F4-class MCUs, exposing clock/reset enables, prescalers, and related control/status registers.
Memory-mapped register block for a GPIO port, including mode, type, speed, pull-up/down, input/output data, bit set/reset, lock, and alternate function registers.
Memory-mapped register block for a USART/UART peripheral, including status, data, baud rate, control, and prescaler registers.

functions.name: spin
functions.signature: static inline void spin(volatile uint32_t count)
functions.description: Busy-wait loop that spins for approximately count iterations. Useful for very short, non-precise delays in bare-metal code.
requirements: count may be any 32-bit value; larger values take longer to return
This is a blocking, CPU-busy delay; it does not sleep or yield and timing is not precise and depends on CPU frequency

functions.name: systick_init
functions.description: Initializes the Cortex-M SysTick timer with the given reload value (ticks) and enables it along with the SYSCFG clock. If ticks is out of the 24-bit SysTick range, the function returns without changing configuration.
requirements: ticks must be in the range 1..0xFFFFFF for the configuration to take effect (SysTick is 24-bit)
Caller should pass a reload value computed for the desired tick rate at the current CPU clock (FREQ)
This function directly accesses SYSTICK and RCC registers; it must be called in a context where those peripherals are present (Cortex-M with STM32-style RCC)

functions.name: gpio_set_mode
functions.signature: static inline void gpio_set_mode(uint16_t pin, uint8_t mode)
functions.description: Configures the GPIO mode for the specified pin. It enables the GPIO bank clock and sets the pin’s MODER field to the provided mode (input/output/alternate/analog).
requirements: pin must be encoded with the PIN(bankChar, pinNumber) macro used by this HAL
mode must be one of: 0 (GPIO_MODE_INPUT), 1 (GPIO_MODE_OUTPUT), 2 (GPIO_MODE_AF), or 3 (GPIO_MODE_ANALOG)
Target GPIO bank must exist on the device; the function writes to RCC->AHB1ENR and the GPIOx MODER register

functions.name: gpio_set_af
functions.signature: static inline void gpio_set_af(uint16_t pin, uint8_t af_num)
functions.description: Selects the alternate function (AF) for the specified GPIO pin by programming the AFR register for that pin.
requirements: pin must be encoded with the PIN(bankChar, pinNumber) macro used by this HAL
af_num must be in the range 0..15 (the AFR field is 4 bits)
The pin should be configured to alternate-function mode (GPIO_MODE_AF) via gpio_set_mode prior to use
Target GPIO bank/pin must support the requested AF as per the MCU datasheet

functions.name: gpio_write
functions.signature: static inline void gpio_write(uint16_t pin, bool val)
functions.description: Sets or resets a GPIO pin by writing to the BSRR register. Writes a 1 to the set bit when val is true, or to the reset bit when val is false.
requirements: pin must be encoded with the PIN(bankChar, pinNumber) macro used by this HAL
The pin should be configured as output or as an AF output for changes to take effect
Target GPIO bank must exist; function writes to GPIOx->BSRR

functions.name: uart_init
functions.signature: static inline void uart_init(struct uart *uart, unsigned long baud)
functions.description: Initializes a UART peripheral for basic TX/RX with the specified baud rate. Enables the corresponding APB clock, configures the default TX/RX pins to AF mode with AF7, programs BRR based on FREQ, and sets UE, RE, TE in CR1.
requirements: uart must point to a valid UART instance, expected to be one of UART1, UART2, or UART3 defined by this HAL
baud must be non-zero to avoid division by zero when computing BRR
The default pin mappings used are: UART1: PA9/PA10, UART2: PA2/PA3, UART3: PD8/PD9, all with AF7; the target MCU must support these mappings
FREQ must reflect the UART peripheral clock frequency for the computed BRR to be correct
This function reconfigures pins and UART registers; it should be called before transmitting/receiving

functions.name: uart_write_byte
functions.signature: static inline void uart_write_byte(struct uart *uart, uint8_t byte)
functions.description: Transmits a single byte over the specified UART. Blocks until the transmit data register is empty (TXE set) after writing the byte.
requirements: uart must point to an initialized UART peripheral
This call busy-waits on the TXE flag; it is blocking and assumes polling mode
Hardware must be clocked/enabled; otherwise the wait may never complete

functions.name: uart_write_buf
functions.signature: static inline void uart_write_buf(struct uart *uart, char *buf, size_t len)
functions.description: Transmits len bytes from the buffer over the specified UART by repeatedly calling uart_write_byte.
requirements: uart must point to an initialized UART peripheral
If len > 0, buf must point to a readable memory region of at least len bytes
This function is blocking and performs polled transmission; it loops until all bytes are sent

functions.name: uart_read_ready
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the UART has received data available to read (RXNE set), otherwise returns 0.
requirements: uart must point to a valid UART peripheral
Caller should check the return value before calling uart_read_byte to avoid reading when no data is present

functions.name: uart_read_byte
functions.description: Reads and returns the least significant 8 bits from the UART data register (DR). Intended to be called after uart_read_ready indicates data availability.
requirements: uart must point to a valid UART peripheral
Caller should ensure data is available (e.g., via uart_read_ready) before calling to avoid reading invalid/old data
Reading DR may clear the RXNE flag on some MCUs; handle accordingly in caller logic

functions.name: timer_expired
functions.signature: static inline bool timer_expired(uint32_t *t, uint32_t prd, uint32_t now)
functions.description: Periodic timer helper. Tracks expiration using a state variable at *t, a desired period prd, and the current time now. Returns true when the timer expires and updates *t to the next expiration, handling wrap-around of the time base.
requirements: t must be a non-NULL pointer to a uint32_t used as persistent state across calls
now and prd must use the same time base units (e.g., ticks) and now should be a monotonically increasing 32-bit counter that may wrap
If *t is zero on first call, the function initializes it to now + prd
A prd of 0 effectively causes immediate expiration on each call (tight loop behavior)

unharnessable_functions.name: systick_init
unharnessable_functions.reason: Directly accesses memory-mapped SYSTICK and RCC registers at fixed addresses, which are not present in the fuzzer environment and could crash.

unharnessable_functions.name: gpio_set_mode
unharnessable_functions.reason: Writes to RCC/GPIO memory-mapped registers based on a hardware-encoded pin, which is not safe or meaningful without the MCU hardware.

unharnessable_functions.name: gpio_set_af
unharnessable_functions.reason: Programs GPIO AFR fields via memory-mapped registers using encoded pins; without hardware this risks invalid memory access and cannot be validated.

unharnessable_functions.name: gpio_write
unharnessable_functions.reason: Manipulates GPIO BSRR in memory-mapped I/O for specific banks; absent hardware this is unsafe and untestable.

unharnessable_functions.name: uart_init
unharnessable_functions.reason: Enables clocks and reconfigures GPIO/UART registers tied to specific MCU addresses; without hardware this may access invalid memory and block.

unharnessable_functions.name: uart_write_byte
unharnessable_functions.reason: Performs a blocking wait on the TXE flag; without hardware support it may never complete, causing the fuzzer to hang.

unharnessable_functions.name: uart_write_buf
unharnessable_functions.reason: Loops on uart_write_byte and can block indefinitely without hardware TXE transitions, making it unsafe for the fuzzer.
